examples.label: Build the installed-package list
examples.command: apt list --installed | tr "/" " " | cut -d" " -f1,3 | sed 's/[0-9]://g' | tee -a installed_pkgs.list

examples.label: Cross-reference each package against GTFOBins
examples.command: for i in $(curl -s https://gtfobins.github.io/gtfobins.json | jq -r 'keys[]'); do if grep -q "$i" installed_pkgs.list; then echo "Check GTFO: $i"; fi; done

notes: Automates the tedious step: which installed binaries have a documented GTFOBins escape. Pair the hits with sudo -l and SUID results - a GTFOBins binary that's also SUID or sudo-allowed is an instant win.

recommended.note: Check which GTFOBins hits are SUID.
Check which GTFOBins hits are sudo-allowed.

name: Enumeration - GTFOBins Cross-Reference
command: for i in $(curl -s https://gtfobins.github.io/gtfobins.json | jq -r 'keys[]'); do if grep -q "$i" installed_pkgs.list; then echo "Check GTFO: $i"; fi; done
description: Cross-references your installed-packages list against GTFOBins to auto-flag binaries with known shell-escape / SUID / sudo abuse techniques.

defense.why_it_works: GTFOBins documents Unix binaries that can be exploited via sudo, SUID, or capabilities to break out of restricted environments or escalate privileges. Cross-referencing installed packages against the GTFOBins list quickly identifies exploitable binaries present on the system.
defense.prerequisites: Shell access. Ability to query installed packages and access GTFOBins API or local copy.
defense.impact: Identifies privilege escalation vectors from legitimate installed binaries (vim, python3, find, less, tee, etc.) that can be abused with SUID bits or sudo permissions.
defense.detection: curl request to gtfobins.github.io API from target (unusual outbound from server). Enumeration of installed packages en masse. SIEM: rapid package listing by non-admin user.
defense.artifacts: Web proxy log (outbound GET to gtfobins.github.io from server) | Process log (apt list executed by non-admin)
defense.prevention: Audit and remove unnecessary SUID/SGID bits from binaries. Review sudo rules to ensure no GTFOBins-listed binaries are granted without restriction (NOPASSWD, ALL). Minimize installed packages (reduce attack surface). Use AppArmor/SELinux profiles to restrict what GTFOBins-listed binaries can do.
defense.misconfiguration: SUID bit set on binaries listed in GTFOBins (vim, python3, find, nmap, awk) without operational necessity. Sudo rules grant ALL or NOPASSWD to these binaries.
defense.vulnerable_config:
# Over-permissive sudo rule
htb-student ALL=(ALL) NOPASSWD: /usr/bin/vim

# Unnecessary SUID on vim
-rwsr-xr-x 1 root root /usr/bin/vim.basic
defense.secure_config:
# Audit SUID binaries regularly
find / -perm /4000 -type f 2>/dev/null

# Remove unnecessary SUID
chmod u-s /usr/bin/vim.basic

# Restrict sudo to specific necessary commands only
# Never grant unrestricted sudo to GTFOBins-listed binaries
